title: SMART Assessment
metaDescription: SMART assessment at Rosehill College — what the assessment involves, why it matters for your child, and how students can prepare for it.

sections.heading: SMART Assessment
sections.lede: The SMART (Student Monitoring, Assessment and Reporting Tool) is the new online assessment being introduced across schools in Aotearoa New Zealand from 2026, replacing e-asTTle. The first round ran from 4–15 May, and the second round will take place from 14 October to 5 November 2026.

sections.heading: SMART Familiarisation Site (Recommended First Step)
sections.html:
Students are encouraged to explore the SMART platform before completing the assessment.

**[SMART Familiarisation Site](https://familiarisation.smart.education.govt.nz/pages/fam-nzc)**

This site allows students to:

* Try sample questions
* Become familiar with the assessment format
* Build confidence before the actual assessment

items.text: The first round ran from Monday 4 to Friday 15 May. The second round will take place from 14 October to 5 November 2026.
Students complete the assessment in a supervised school setting, usually in their class groups.
Assessments are completed online — students should bring their own device. Parents can let Kaitiaki/Head of House know if a device needs to be booked. Please do so by 4th May.

sections.heading: What is the SMART Assessment?
sections.html: The SMART (Student Monitoring, Assessment and Reporting Tool) is a new online assessment. It is being introduced across schools in Aotearoa New Zealand from 2026. SMART provides clear and consistent information about student progress in: * Reading * Writing * Mathematics It replaces the e-asTTle assessment and is aligned with the new curriculum. Teachers use SMART results to track student progress and support conversations with students and whānau. Parents and caregivers will receive information about their child's progress through our reporting processes.

sections.heading: Purpose of the Assessment
sections.html:
SMART is a learning check designed to:

* Help teachers understand what students already know
* Identify next learning steps
* Provide information to parents and caregivers

The focus is on progress and improvement over time, rather than a single result.

sections.heading: How the Assessment Runs
sections.html: Assessments are completed online — students should bring their own device. Each assessment typically takes 30–45 minutes. Questions may include: * Multiple choice * Short written responses * Interactive tasks (for example, drag-and-drop tools) Students complete the assessment in a supervised school setting, usually in their class groups. Parents can let Kaitiaki/Head of House know if a device needs to be booked. Please do so before the assessment window.

sections.heading: Further Information
sections.text: For more information about SMART, please refer to the official guidance from the Ministry of Education. If you have any questions, please contact the college.
